_why: Every word here is loaded before the model's first tool result, and it is loaded on every question. A weekly health check carried 10,018 words of instructions in 1.13.2; four rules were written nine to fifteen times over, and the one case that would not pass three runs of three failed on the rule written nine times. Repetition is not enforcement. See docs/incidents.md, 2026-09-17.
_howToRaise: Do not. A skill that needs more room is a skill with a rule that belongs in references/run-protocol.md, a call detail that belongs in references/mcp-calls.md, or a story that belongs in docs/incidents.md. Raise a cap only when a genuinely new procedure arrives, and say so in the commit.

contextBudget._why: What a scheduled weekly report loads before it can do anything. This is the number that matters to the model, and the one the caps above exist to hold.

_capNotes.seal-copilot/skills/create-alert/SKILL.m: Set at 1200, not the 1100 default. It came from 2,393: the rule grammar and the four families moved to references/alert-grammar.md (shared with check-alerts), the false-alarm arithmetic became `calc false-alarm`, and the routines story went to docs/incidents.md. What is left is a natural-language parse, a statistical refusal and a rule lifecycle, each instruction distinct. The last 85 words would have to come out of something that matters.
_capNotes.seal-copilot/skills/seal-copilot/SKILL.m: Set at 1500. It is the methodology skill: 17 operating rules, vertical detection and the routing table every other skill depends on.
_capNotes.seal-copilot/skills/seal-copilot/referen: Set at 1000. This file replaced 3,201 words of duplication across fifteen skills and also carries the calculator table and the seal-state fallback for surfaces with no filesystem. Because every skill reads it, the guard that matters is contextBudget below, which counts what a weekly actually loads; this per-file cap only stops it becoming a dumping ground.
